The Peaceful Death of the Righteous Few: the Ungodliness of the Many: a Believing Remnant Shall Survive the General Judgments of the Nation, and Be Restored by Him Who Creates Peace.</title> <div sID="gen16250" type="x-p"/> In the midst of the excesses of the unfaithful watchmen (<reference osisRef="Isa.56.10">Is 56:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.11.12">11, 12</reference>), most of the few that are godly perish: partly by vexation at the prevailing ungodliness; partly by violent death in persecution: prophetical of the persecuting times of Manasseh, before God's judgments in causing the captivity in Babylon; and again those in the last age of the Church, before the final judgments on the apostasy (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.21.16">2Ki 21:16</reference>; Mt 23:29-35, 37; <reference osisRef="Rev.11.17">Re 11:17</reference>). The Hebrew for "perisheth," and "is taken away," expresses a violent death (<reference osisRef="Mic.7.2">Mi 7:2</reference>).<div eID="gen16250" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16251" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9392"/><hi type="bold">1. no man layeth it to heart--</hi>as a public calamity.<div eID="gen16251" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16252" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">merciful men--</hi>rather, godly men; the subjects of mercy.<div eID="gen16252" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16253" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">none considering--</hi>namely, what was the design of Providence in removing the godly.<div eID="gen16253" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16254" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from the evil--</hi>Hebrew, from the face of the evil, that is, both from the moral evil on every side (<reference osisRef="Isa.56.10-Isa.56.12">Is 56:10-12</reference>), and from the evils about to come in punishment of the national sins, foreign invasions, &c. (<reference osisRef="Isa.56.9">Is 56:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.57.13">57:13</reference>). So Ahijah's death is represented as a blessing conferred on him by God for his piety (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.14.10-1Kgs.14.13">1Ki 14:10-13</reference>; see also <reference osisRef="2Kgs.22.20">2Ki 22:20</reference>). <div eID="gen16254" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 57 Is 57:1-21 . The Peaceful Death of the Righteous Few: the Ungodliness of the Many: a Believing Remnant Shall Survive the General Judgments of the Nation, and Be Restored by Him Who Creates Peace. In the midst of the excesses of the unfaithful watchmen ( Is 56:10 , 11, 12 ), most of the few that are godly perish: partly by vexation at the prevailing ungodliness; partly by violent death in persecution: prophetical of the persecuting times of Manasseh, before God's judgments in causing the captivity in Babylon; and again those in the last age of the Church, before the final judgments on the apostasy ( 2Ki 21:16 ; Mt 23:29-35, 37; Re 11:17 ). The Hebrew for "perisheth," and "is taken away," expresses a violent death ( Mi 7:2 ). 1. no man layeth it to heart-- as a public calamity. merciful men-- rather, godly men; the subjects of mercy. none considering-- namely, what was the design of Providence in removing the godly. from the evil-- Hebrew, from the face of the evil, that is, both from the moral evil on every side ( Is 56:10-12 ), and from the evils about to come in punishment of the national sins, foreign invasions, &c. ( Is 56:9 ; 57:13 ). So Ahijah's death is represented as a blessing conferred on him by God for his piety ( 1Ki 14:10-13 ; see also 2Ki 22:20 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9399"/><div sID="gen16273" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9399"/>8. "Remembrance," that is, memorials of thy idolatry: the objects which thou holdest in remembrance. They hung up household tutelary gods "behind the doors"; the very place where God has directed them to write His laws "on the posts and gates" (<reference osisRef="Deut.6.9">De 6:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.11.20">11:20</reference>); a curse, too, was pronounced on putting up an image "in a secret place" (<reference osisRef="Deut.27.15">De 27:15</reference>).<div eID="gen16273" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16274" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">discovered thyself--</hi>image from an adulteress.<div eID="gen16274" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16275" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">enlarged ... bed--</hi>so as to receive the more paramours.<div eID="gen16275" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16276" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">made ... covenant--</hi>with idols: in open violation of thy "covenant" with God (<reference osisRef="Exod.19.5">Ex 19:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.23.32">23:32</reference>). Or, "hast made assignations with them for thyself" [Horsley].<div eID="gen16276" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16277" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thy bed ... their bed--</hi>The Jews' sin was twofold; they resorted to places of idolatry ("their bed"), and they received idols into the temple of God ("thy bed").<div eID="gen16277" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16278" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">where--</hi>rather, "ever since that" [Horsley]. The Hebrew for "where" means "room" (Margin), a place; therefore, translate, "thou hast provided a place for it" (for "their bed"), namely, by admitting idolatrous altars in thy land [Barnes]; or "thou choosest a (convenient) place for thyself" in their bed [Maurer] (<reference osisRef="Isa.56.5">Is 56:5</reference>). <div eID="gen16278" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9400"/><div sID="gen16279" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9400"/><hi type="bold">9. the king--</hi>the idol which they came to worship, perfumed with oil, like harlots (<reference osisRef="Jer.4.30">Jr 4:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.23.16">Eze 23:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.23.40">40</reference>). So "king" means idol (<reference osisRef="Amos.5.26">Am 5:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.1.5">Zep 1:5</reference>); (malcham meaning "king") [Rosenmuller]. navigation_sections.title: CHAPTER 57
navigation_sections.content_plain: CHAPTER 57 Is 57:1-21 . The Peaceful Death of the Righteous Few: the Ungodliness of the Many: a Believing Remnant Shall Survive the General Judgments of the Nation, and Be Restored by Him Who Creates Peace. In the midst of the excesses of the unfaithful watchmen ( Is 56:10 , 11, 12 ), most of the few that are godly perish: partly by vexation at the prevailing ungodliness; partly by violent death in persecution: prophetical of the persecuting times of Manasseh, before God's judgments in causing the captivity in Babylon; and again those in the last age of the Church, before the final judgments on the apostasy ( 2Ki 21:16 ; Mt 23:29-35, 37; Re 11:17 ). The Hebrew for "perisheth," and "is taken away," expresses a violent death ( Mi 7:2 ).

The Peaceful Death of the Righteous Few: the Ungodliness of the Many: a Believing Remnant Shall Survive the General Judgments of the Nation, and Be Restored by Him Who Creates Peace.</title> <div sID="gen16250" type="x-p"/> In the midst of the excesses of the unfaithful watchmen (<reference osisRef="Isa.56.10">Is 56:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.11.12">11, 12</reference>), most of the few that are godly perish: partly by vexation at the prevailing ungodliness; partly by violent death in persecution: prophetical of the persecuting times of Manasseh, before God's judgments in causing the captivity in Babylon; and again those in the last age of the Church, before the final judgments on the apostasy (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.21.16">2Ki 21:16</reference>; Mt 23:29-35, 37; <reference osisRef="Rev.11.17">Re 11:17</reference>). The Hebrew for "perisheth," and "is taken away," expresses a violent death (<reference osisRef="Mic.7.2">Mi 7:2</reference>).<div eID="gen16250" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16251" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9392"/>
